sentences.text:
This Appeal Coming On For Admission This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:

Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.M.B.Ryakha, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.L.Sreekanta Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.
Dissatisfied with the amount awarded as compensation and further disputing the aspect of contributory negligence, this appeal is preferred by the claimant.
Challenge in this appeal is that an order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru in MVC.No.671/2019 dated 05.03.2022.
As NC: 2024:KHC:32431 against the claim for Rs.15,00,000/- in total, the Tribunal through the impugned order, awarded a sum of Rs.5,41,000/- as compensation.

Attributing contributory negligence to an extent of 10% to the appellant, the Tribunal fastened the liability to an extent of 90% upon the driver of the Mahindra Tractor which is involved in the accident and directed the respondents to make good the loss to the appellant.
Thus, the respondents were fastened with the liability to a tune of Rs.4,86,900/-.

3. Arguing in respect of merits of the matter, Sri.M.B.Ryakha, learned counsel for the appellant submits that without there being any evidence, the Tribunal attributed contributory negligence on part of the appellant which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel states that by producing all the relevant record, the appellant established that the driver of the Mahindra Tractor which is involved in the accident is at fault.
Learned counsel thereby seeks to pass necessary orders in that regard.

The manner of happening of accident as per the version of the appellant is that on 07.04.2019 at about 08.45 am, while he was proceeding on his two wheeler on Madhugiri-Sira road and when he reached near Sira gate auto stand, a Mahidra Tractor bearing registration No.KA- 06-TA-5631 came from back side driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed and dashed Shabbir Khana vs Nagendrappa on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97784437/
2 against him, due to which he fell down and sustained injuries.

5. Sri.L.Sreekanta Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.2 did not deny the fact that the Police after investigation came to a conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence driving of the driver of the Tractor.
No evidence whatsoever is produced by the respondents to establish that the appellant was at fault or that he contributed to the accident.

Thus, without there being any substantive proof with regard to the negligence on part of the appellant, as rightly contended by Sri.M.B.Ryakha, learned counsel for the appellant, the NC: 2024:KHC:32431 Tribunal attributed contributory negligence on part of the appellant.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that no liability can be fastened against the appellant.

6. Coming to the quantum of amount that is awarded as compensation, the Tribunal taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained and the aspect of the disability, awarded compensation under following heads:
1. Pain and sufferings 60,000/-
2. Medical expenses 57,000/- 3 Food, attendant and conveyance 60,000/-
charges 4. Loss of future income due to 2,96,000/-
permanent disability 5. Loss of enjoyment of life due to 15,000/-
injuries 6. Loss of income during the period of 28,000/-
treatment 7.

Future medical expenses 25,000/-
 Total 5,41,000/-
 NC: 2024:KHC:32431 7.
It is not in dispute that the appellant sustained fracture of both bones of right leg.
Equally, it is not in dispute that the appellant underwent surgery with CRIF with IMIL nailing.

Also it is established Shabbir Khana vs Nagendrappa on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97784437/
3 that when there was non-union of bones, the appellant underwent dynamization and fibulectomy.

sentences.text: 8. Having considered such an extensive treatment taken by the appellant, this Court is of the view that the appellant would have taken bed rest at least for a period of three months.
However, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.28,000/- only towards 'loss of income' during the treatment period.
Taking the notional income of the appellant as Rs.14,000/-, this Court is of the view that 'loss of income during laid up period' comes to Rs.42,000/- (Rs.14,000 X 3) in total.
Thus, the enhancement would be Rs.14,000/-.
This Court is also of the view that the amount of compensation granted under all other heads is reasonable and therefore, requires no interference.

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:32431 ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The amount that is awarded as compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru through orders in MVC.No.671/2019 dated 05.03.2022 is enhanced by Rs.14,000/-.
iii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the entire compensation that is awarded by the Tribunal together with the enhanced amount.
v) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the sum awarded within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
vi) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
